messages:
Jordan: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern in the tenant cost heatmap this morning, some tenants showing large 'cache savings' credits but overall token cost still spiking. dashboard link: https://console.redwood/inference/costs/heatmap :eyes:
Marie: Can you paste the query or a permalink? which breakdown? per-route or per-model?
Jordan: Per-tenant > per-route view. Quick permalink: https://console.redwood/inference/costs/heatmap?mode=tenant&breakdown=route&time=1h
Jordan: The odd bit is a stack where eviction credits jump at the same time as a ratelimit surge. Looks like credits are applied but the effective token cost still tallies the evicted tokens somewhere.
Sam: That sounds like double-counting between prefetch-credit reconciliation and the marginal-cost exporter. Could be a race when the eviction event comes in after billing aggregation window.
Tay: Are we sure it's not a sticky-routing fallback -> model downgrade causing higher per-token cost? fallback spikes + eviction credits could mask it in the UI.
Jordan: Good call. I sliced by model SKU and saw small-model SKU usage up, but total token count is same. snippet I used:
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, route_id, model_sku, sum(tokens) as tokens, sum(eviction_credits) as credits
FROM billing_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY 1,2,3
ORDER BY tokens desc
LIMIT 50;
```
Marie: Can you run with `include_prefetch=true`? last time prefetch credits were stored as negative tokens in one stream and positive credits in another, causing the rollup to show both.
Jordan: running now... :hourglass_flowing_sand:
cost-alert-bot: ALERT: tenant=tenant-42 cost-delta=+42% window=1h rule=eviction-credit-variance
Jordan: result: tenant-42 has 18k tokens, eviction_credits = 11k, but model-cost_raw shows cost_for_tokens = cost(18k) + prefetch_rebilling(9k) -> looks duplicated.
Sam: Yeah that matches the race. The reconciler does a best-effort join by `request_id`, but when requests are evicted early we emit an eviction event that the batcher reconciler sometimes misses if events arrive out-of-order.
Tay: Operational question — do quotas/ratelimits trigger evictions? If so, eviction events may be correlated with ratelimit bursts. That would explain the temporal overlap.
Jordan: Confirmed: we see `evict=true` flagged in batch logs at the same epoch as `quota-exceeded` traces.
Denise: From Console UX perspective, customers see negative cache savings and wonder why invoice still high. We should show a separate "Eviction recharges" line in the per-tenant breakdown so the arithmetic is clearer.
Marie: Proposal: Add a reconciliation flag in telemetry -> `reconciled_by_reconciler=true|false` and surface unreconciled events in the console with a tooltip: "may be double-counted until reconciliation completes".
Sam: Longer fix: make reconciler idempotent by writing reconciliation markers atomically to the billing ledger (two-phase): write provisional, then finalize once both credit & debit seen. That avoids transient double-counts. But it's a non-trivial migration.
Tay: Short-term mitigations: 1) In UI, split out `prefetch_credit` and `eviction_recharge` so users can see both lines. 2) In alerts, tighten rule to only fire if net_token_cost increases by >X% for 15m after credits.
Jordan: I'm going to open a ticket with reproducer and query + sample trace. Also pushing a tiny console UX patch that adds an "Eviction recharge" series to heatmap (non-breaking).
Denise: Great — include copy for tooltip explaining reconciliation latency. We'll QA with tenant-42 and add to release notes.
Sam: Assigning engineering follow-up: ENGPLAT-1789 (reconciler idempotency), Jordan please add logs and a failing unit test for the out-of-order arrival.
Jordan: Done. PR draft: https://git.redwood/engplat/pulls/4567 (UI patch). Will schedule a canary behind flag `ui.eviction_recharge=true` and roll for 1h.
Marie: For telemetry, let's increase sample-rate for eviction events from 1% -> 5% for an hour so we can trace reconciling failures in prod. I'll run the sampling job.
cost-alert-bot: NOTE: sampling-change applied: eviction_event_sample_rate=5% by Marie at 1712350200
Tay: Also, check routing policy: if fallback routing to cheaper model is happening frequently, we may want to expose per-route model fallback percentage in the cost panel.
Jordan: Agreed. Action items: (1) UI patch (Jordan) behind flag, (2) sampling bump (Marie) — done, (3) reconciler ticket (Sam) assigned, (4) UX tooltip + release note (Denise). Will follow up after canary.
Denise: Thanks — please post a short blameless incident note once we confirm root cause so CS has copy for tenants who ask. :+1:
Jordan: Will do. I'll update thread when canary results in 1h.
